item.title: Arsenal could make move for Monaco attacker in January
item.description: Arsenal could make move for Monaco attacker in January Paris Brunner has been one of the finest young talents in Europe since breaking through at Borussia Dortmund, and he has been on Monaco’s books since 2024. The wonderkid is beginning to receive regular game time and is increasingly impressing in France, leading to links with a move to Arsenal in future transfer windows. The Gunners view Brunner as one of the top young players in Europe for his age group and will do their best to add him to their squad when a window opens. His development at Monaco has strengthened their belief that he could become a valuable long term addition. Arsenal Eye January Move Monaco are aware that they have a top player on their hands and have done their best to keep him at the club. However, they could find it difficult to prevent a transfer if a major club decides to move decisively. As revealed by Team Talk , Arsenal are serious about the 20-year-old and could make a move as soon as the January transfer window opens. The Gunners have been impressed by what they have seen when monitoring him, and they recognise that waiting until the summer could make a deal more difficult. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Why January Could Suit Arsenal By the summer, more clubs are likely to enter the race for Brunner’s signature, increasing competition and potentially raising his price. Moving in January would allow Arsenal to steal a march on rival suitors and secure one of Europe’s most promising young attackers before the market becomes more crowded. For Arsenal, the opportunity is clear. If they can convince Monaco to sell and persuade Brunner that North London is the right next step, they would be adding a highly rated talent with significant room to develop. Acting early could be crucial to winning the race for his signature. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Astros pitcher Tatsuya Imai makes obvious $18 million contract option decision
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Astros pitcher Tatsuya Imai makes obvious $18 million contract option decision appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Houston Astros right-hander Tatsuya Imai has reached a contract decision after an uneven first major league season that included time in the rotation and bullpen. The former Saitama Seibu Lions pitcher joined the Astros before the 2026 campaign on a three-year, $54 million contract with opt-outs after the 2026 and 2027 seasons. His debut year ended with a 6-4 record and 4.93 ERA across 23 appearances, including 15 starts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The agreement gave Imai an opportunity to revisit his future after his first season, with two years and $36 million remaining. USA Today’s Bob Nightengale relayed Imai’s decision Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, crediting an earlier report from the New York Post’s Jon Heyman. “Zero surprise, but struggling Astros starter Tatsuya Imai will exercise his $18 million player option and return to the Astros, as @JonHeyman said.” Imai’s return keeps him in Houston for 2027, with another opportunity to opt out after next season. He struck out 97 batters and issued 51 walks over 76 2/3 innings in 2026, illustrating both his ability to miss bats and his command difficulties. The right-hander spent time on the injured list with arm fatigue during the first half before shifting to relief work in late July. Eight of his 23 appearances came out of the bullpen, and his workload declined down the stretch. Imai made the Astros’ postseason roster but did not pitch in the American League Wild Card Series. His contract decision establishes his salary for next season without settling how Houston will use him. The Astros now retain a pitcher with experience in both roles, while Imai enters another season with a chance to improve on his MLB debut and establish a more consistent pitching role.

item.description: Carabao Cup quarterfinal draw: Fixtures, ball numbers, key dates for next stage of 2026/27 EFL knockout tournament originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026/27 Carabao Cup steams ahead unabated as England's secondary knockout competition plows into the quarterfinal round of action. The field has been further carved down from 16 to just eight clubs remaining after the conclusion of the fourth round, and quarterfinal participants are now aiming for a spot in the two-legged final four on the horizon. Defending champions Manchester City are still alive in the competition hoping to secure yet another EFL Cup title, something they've won in five of the last nine seasons. Last year's Premier League title-winners Arsenal, who fell in last year's final to Man City, were aiming to secure their first League Cup championship since 1993 but found themselves stunned in the fourth round by League Two side Fleetwood Town who stood 84 places below them in the English football pyramid. The Sporting News brings you the information for the quarterfinal round, including the draw results, ball numbers, what clubs are left in the competition, and when the matches will eventually take place after a significant layoff. That match will kick off at 8 p.m. local time (4 p.m. ET), meaning the draw will be held in the evening following the final whistle, around 10:15 p.m. local time (6:15 p.m. ET). item.title: Fleetwood to face Everton in EFL Cup quarters
item.description: Fleetwood Town had never gone past the third round before this season [Getty Images] League Two side Fleetwood Town will face Everton at Highbury in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup. The lowest-ranked side left in the competition have already made history by reaching the last eight after they stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties on Tuesday. Everton confirmed their place in the quarter-finals on Thursday night, with a 3-1 win over Newcastle in an all-Premier League tie. Holders Manchester City will host the only other non-Premier League side - League One Bradford City - at Etihad Stadium after they needed penalties to get past Brighton in the last 16. The other two fixtures will be all-Premier League affairs with Liverpool, who also required a penalty shootout to beat Chelsea , hosting Bournemouth and Crystal Palace taking on Sunderland at Selhurst Park. Quarter-final fixtures will take place in the week commencing 14 December. item.title: Charley Hull Opens Up About Personal Life and Her Viral Moment
item.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Women’s Golf Journal reports that Charley Hull’s official career prize money totals over $11.5 million. Among today’s LPGA Tour players, she ranks as one of the most successful due to this amount. She turned professional at age 16 and won Rookie of the Year in 2013. Her path to wealth involves nine professional tournament wins and major finishes. Hull also secured key equipment and apparel deals that add to her income stream. The English golfer built her bank account through steady play and bold choices off the course. In 2019, she secured a contract with TaylorMade Golf, which she later renewed in 2022. Her reported commercial portfolio includes Rockstar Energy and Malbon Golf. These partnerships reflect her appeal beyond just golf, as noted by Women’s Golf Journal. Brands pay for her personality as much as her swing speed. Personal Struggles and Public Growth Hull has been open about her battle with ADHD and past struggles with substance use. She told Heavy Sports, according to Heavy.com , “I had a few stressful things going on in my life, and I got prescribed for some Xanaxes, and I felt like I was getting addicted to Xanaxes.” The golfer later stopped vaping and switched to smoking cigarettes to smoke less. She eventually decided to quit smoking entirely after a specific moment of clarity. She explained her decision to stop, saying, “And then it comes to a day where I was very stressed and I was smoking a lot, and I thought you know what, that’s it, I’m done.” Hull made a bet with a friend and has not touched cigarettes since. She now uses nicotine pouches to help her cope. “Made a bet with my friend and I haven’t touched them (since) and that’s when I started the nicotine pouches and that’s helped me, (it) just helps me sometimes,” Hull added. The Viral Moment That Changed Everything A viral video of Hull smoking on the course actually boosted her popularity rather than hurting it. Her friends, Nelly Korda and Megan Khang, told her she had gone viral for smoking. Hull admitted she did not realize the scale of the reaction until she checked her phone later. “I was like that’s crazy, I didn’t realize how big it was until I turned my phone on a few days later on my Instagram and I gained about 200,000 followers.” This surge in followers likely increased her value to active sponsors like Malbon Golf. The brand signed her in 2024 for an apparel deal. Her bold style now helps her stand out on the course.

item.title: Charles Leclerc defends Alex Albon after Fernando Alonso's scathing criticism
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has rejected Fernando Alonso's claim that the standard of driving at the back of the grid is low, insisting the level is "very, very high" across the field. Alonso criticised the lower third of the grid after his battle with Williams driver Alex Albon at last weekend's United States Grand Prix and stood by his comments while speaking to the media in Mexico City. "I think the quality of the drivers in the lower third of the grid is very low, as we saw today with Alex," Alonso said after a collision with Albon on the opening lap at the Circuit of the Americas. "So I think we need to improve the car and start a little bit higher up." Asked about the standard of the grid during the drivers' press conference in Mexico, Leclerc dismissed the Spaniard's comments. "I think it’s very high. I think it’s very, very high. Just like I was saying earlier, most of the grid, we grew up together in karting," Leclerc said. "Alex was up there and was actually a driver I was looking up to. He was always one or two categories above me, but he was exceptional." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Leclerc, who is currently fifth in the drivers' standings, added that the difference between the front and the back of the field comes down to machinery. "Today, I’m sure that the level of the grid is super, super high, whether it’s in the back, in the middle or in the front. The only things that change is obviously the race car that we are driving, but the standards are very high," the Monegasque said. Albon, who joined Leclerc in the press conference, also disagreed with Alonso's assessment. "I have huge respect for Fernando, I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid, and obviously it’s not nice to hear those comments in many ways," the Williams driver said. "You’re racing someone that you look up to, but at the same time, I don’t agree. It’s as simple as that. "I think the level is strong up and down the grid. I think 10, 15 years ago, the back half of the grid wasn’t the way it is now. We don’t have paid drivers anymore." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Grealish dropped by Everton after 'breach of club discipline'
item.description: Jack Grealish has featured six times for Everton this season [Getty Images] Jack Grealish was left out of Everton's Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle United on Thursday "due to a breach of club discipline". Everton did not disclose any further details but it is understood to arise from an unauthorised absence from training. Everton overcame Grealish's absence to win 3-1 and book a quarter-final tie at League Two Fleetwood Town. England winger Grealish, 31, is on loan at Everton from Premier League rivals Manchester City. He spent a large chunk of last season with the Toffees under a similar arrangement, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances, before sustaining a season-ending foot injury in January. Grealish came on as a substitute during City's 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal at Wembley in August. The former Aston Villa player, who cost City £100m in 2021, also featured as a substitute during City's 2-1 win over Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the Premier League season. He returned to Everton before the transfer window closed and has featured five times for them this season in the Premier League. item.title: Knicks planning on declining Pacome Dadiet’s $5.37 million contract option
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Knicks planning on declining Pacome Dadiet’s $5.37 million contract option appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After two relatively underwhelming seasons, the New York Knicks are reportedly declining third-year guard Pacome Dadiet’s contract option for the 2027-28 season, as per Shams Charania of ESPN. The decision will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent at the end of this season, although Charania did hint that this does not close the door on the French native ultimately returning to the team. The No. 25 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft by the Knicks, Pacome Dadiet was still playing on his rookie scale contract as he entered his third season in the league. If the organization would have picked up his contract option, he would have hit restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Despite being a first round pick, Dadiet has yet to make a meaningful impact on the team. Across his first two seasons in the NBA, he has never averaged more than six minutes per game, while playing in a grand total of 47 games. This year, he’s appeared in only one game for the Knicks in which he played a single minute. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 21-year-old did not suit up in the Knicks’ first three games of the year, before seeing minutes during the team’s blowout win against the Detroit Pistons on Oct. 27. He finished with only one rebound and did not take a shot. Across his first two seasons in the NBA, he holds career averages of 1.7 points and 0.9 rebounds along with splits of 32.8 percent shooting from the field, 26.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 74.3 percent shooting from the free-throw line. item.title: OHSAA removes Glenville from 2026 football playoffs amid investigation
item.description: The Ohio High School Athletic Association has removed Cleveland Glenville from the 2026 football playoffs, the organization announced in an email late Thursday, Oct. 29. The Tarblooders' removal from the Division III, Region 9 postseason came as part of an ongoing investigation into Cleveland Metropolitan School District and inaccurately assigning student participation opportunities to Glenville. It all stems from students at Ginn Academy, which is a non-member magnet school that does not offer sports and is under the control of Cleveland Metropolitan School District. Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year Student-athletes from Ginn Academy are only allowed to participate at the Cleveland school district closest to their residence. What happens in Division III with Glenville football out of the playoffs Glenville's removal knocks out the Tarblooders, who were the No. 12 seed, and pushes No. 12 Hunting Valley University School (6-4) to a Week 12 game against No. 3 Garfield Heights (8-2). “Recently we discovered several irregularities with students going to Ginn Academy and playing football at Glenville, which led us to conduct an audit of the participation opportunities for all fall sports student-athletes at Glenville High School,” OHSAA Executive Director Doug Ute said in the email. “This week we confirmed that many players on Glenville’s football team should have been playing at other schools this season. It will take some time to examine all the information and determine the extent of the violations this season and potentially in previous seasons for all schools and teams within Cleveland Metro.” It's the second time Glenville has been removed from the football playoffs for the same infractions. In October 2018, the Tarblooders were removed and incurred $5,000 fine. They were placed on probation through 2021. Glenville won the Division IV football state championship in 2022, 2023 and 2025 and entered the 2026 playoffs as the No. 5 seed in the Division III, Region 9 playoffs. There is not an exact timetable on the full scope of the investigation and additional penalties, according to the email. item.title: Commanders vs. Eagles Thursday injury report: Javon Kinlaw still out
item.description: It sure looks like the Commanders are going to play Sunday night’s game without Javon Kinlaw . The defensive tackle missed his second practice of the week while dealing with a knee injury. That’s a big deal, considering his impact on the Commanders interior defensive line to this point. There’s always hope that he can recover in time to play the Eagles, and Charles Omenihu ’s return to practice activity theoretically offers some depth if Kinlaw can’t go. Receiver Stefon Diggs was back at practice , as head coach Dan Quinn previously announced, after some veteran rest and despite hand and hamstring issues. That’s a plus for the Commanders, especially with Terry McLaurin out for the foreseeable future . Tight end John Bates missed a second day with a shoulder issue. Not having him available on Sunday, if we get that far, is a sneaky big deal considering his role as a blocker in the pass and run games. Receiver Treylon Burks went from limited to a DNP, which is a bad sign for an already banged up pass-catching corps. Also center Nick Allegretti popped up on the injury report with a back issue. item.title: Suspended UTSA basketball coach passed out in car outside convenience store before DWI arrest
item.description: Austin Claunch, 36, is pictured in a mugshot at the Nueces County jail. He is charged with driving while intoxicated. (Courtesy of the Corpus Christi Police Department) A newly-released police report details the arrest of suspended UTSA men's basketball coach Austin Claunch , who is charged with driving while intoxicated. Corpus Christi police officers found Claunch passed out in a Mercedes on Tuesday in the parking lot of a Stripes convenience store, according to a police report obtained by KENS-TV . The car's engine was running, and one of the doors was open. Officers conducted a field sobriety test before arresting Claunch. A store clerk told officers that Claunch had been "stumbling around" inside the store about 30 minutes earlier, KENS-TV reported. Claunch, 36, was booked into the Nueces County jail Tuesday and released after posting a $1,500 bond, jail officials told the San Antonio Express-News. Claunch led the Roadrunners through practice Wednesday and spoke with local media that afternoon. UTSA athletics director Lisa Campos announced his suspension shortly after 6 p.m. "The university is reviewing the circumstances and will determine appropriate next steps, including the length of his suspension," Campos said in a statement. "UTSA Athletics holds its coaches, staff and student-athletes to high standards of conduct and accountability. We take this matter seriously and will address it in accordance with university policies and procedures." Assistant coach Nick Bowman will serve as acting head coach as the Roadrunners prepare to open their season Monday at San Jose State. In a statement released Wednesday, Claunch apologized and called the incident "a grave error in judgement." "I recognize the responsibility that comes with being a head coach and the example I am expected to set, both on and off the court," he said. "I fell short of those expectations, and for that, I am truly sorry. I take full responsibility for my decisions and am committed to learning from this experience and earning back the trust and confidence of those who have placed their faith in me." item.title: ‘Historic,’ ‘No Caitlin Clark Fan Can Slander Her Again’ – WNBA World Hypes Up Angel Reese’s Performance As Dream Force Game 7 vs. Valkyries
item.description: ‘Historic,’ ‘No Caitlin Clark Fan Can Slander Her Again’ – WNBA World Hypes Up Angel Reese’s Performance As Dream Force Game 7 vs. Valkyries The first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history is officially set after Angel Reese helped the Atlanta Dream defeat the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6. While the controversial early-afternoon start time generated headlines heading into the game, Reese ensured it wouldn’t be the final game of the season, and multiple fans and analysts praised her. WNBA World Praises Angel Reese After Dream Force Game Seven of The Finals Reese was a major contributor in the Dream’s 80-69 win over the Golden State Valkyries, and made history in the process. Legion Hoops noted , “Angel Reese just broke the WNBA record for most rebounds in a Finals series. Historic.” Reese has 78 total rebounds in the series heading into Game 7. She finished Game 6 with 15 points, 14 rebounds, and 6 assists. Reese has re-joined Finals MVP conversations after being criticized following a couple of rough performances. One fan used Reese’s strong performance to spotlight her rivalry with another popular star, saying , “Angel Reese really the best ever. No Caitlin Clark fan can slander her ever again.” The Dream arguably won Game 6 in the first half, as the Valkyries’ perimeter defense struggled and watched multiple players hit big three-point shots. Several fans praised Reese for making a couple of threes during the run. WNBA analyst Noa Dalzell said , “Angel Reese is shooting 44.4% from three in the playoffs, by the way.” One fan said , “Angel Reese adding that 3-point shot took her game to a whole new level.” Another fan said , “Angel Reese finding this level of success and familiarity behind the arc is scary for the league in 2028, man.” Dream Head Coach Karl Smesko’s system relies on centers and forwards stretching the defense by making perimeter shots, something Reese struggled with early in her career. Smesko worked with Reese to overhaul her shooting form to expand her range. Reese said it’s been a frustrating process at times, but she is getting more comfortable at shooting threes and should continue improving as her career progresses. MORE: ‘Sometimes You Try Not to Fan Out’ — 76ers Star Tyrese Maxey Makes Feelings Clear on ‘Really Cool’ Meeting With Caitlin Clark NBA analyst Ryan Kaminski was impressed with Reese’s overall game, saying , “Angel Reese bringing the energy, point forward playmaking, and showing off the development of the jumper.” Dream stars Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray also stepped up in Game 6 to support Reese, and now the organization has the momentum heading back to the Bay Area for a historic game on Halloween. item.title: Brother of former Barcelona star spotted training with Hansi Flick’s squad
item.description: Brother of former Barcelona star spotted training with Hansi Flick’s squad The brother of ex-Barcelona star Pau Víctor was afforded a call-up to training alongside the rest of Hansi Flick’s senior squad on Thursday morning. This comes as the Blaugrana coaching staff work to cover for the ongoing personnel crisis in the club’s defensive ranks. Ahead of their upcoming weekend meeting with Deportivo Alavés, Barca are currently unable to count on any of Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Jules Koundé or Xavi Espart. Amid efforts to bounce back from a pair of successive defeats in all competitions, Hansi Flick has therefore turned his focus towards the academy setup in Catalunya’s capital. And on Thursday, as much gave rise to a new face in the senior setup at the Ciutat Esportiva. As per a report from Diario Sport : ‘Flick tested the reserve team full-back, Guillem Víctor, the novelty of the week, in the last session.’ Víctor, for his part, is a versatile 19-year-old defender, who chiefly lines out at right-back. The Spaniard is the brother of ex-Barcelona frontman Pau, who now plies his club trade in Portugal with SC Braga. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Cundy's 20-year reign as world champion ends
item.description: Cundy won his first Para-cycling world title in 2006 [Getty Images] Great Britain's Jody Cundy's 20-year reign as para cycling's C4 kilo time trial world champion was ended by Australian Korey Boddington at the para cycling track world championships in the Netherlands. Cundy, 48, won the world title in 2006 and had managed to hold onto his rainbow jersey in the 15 world championships since. But battling for his 17th title in the C4 kilo discipline, Cundy had to settle for silver after finishing his kilometre in one minute and 4.93 seconds, a time which Boddington beat by 2.25 seconds on the final run. Before the event, Cundy had said "age was catching up with him" and it would be "hard" to add to his 23 track cycling world titles. Cundy is a nine-time Paralympic champion - with three of his medals coming in para swimming between 1996 and 2000. Elsewhere on day one of the championships, Great Britain's Rebecca Newark took gold in the women's C5 kilo time trial. In the women's B kilo time trial, Britain's Sophie Unwin and pilot Jenny Holl won silver and Elizabeth Jordan and pilot Anna Whitworth Hay claimed bronze. There was silver for British pair Morgan Fice-Noyes and Christopher Latham in the men's 4km pursuit, while Great Britain's Finlay Graham also took bronze in the men's C3 sprint final. item.title: Purdue volleyball's Kenna Wollard provides update on health status
item.description: Coming off an All-American season for an Elite Eight team, Kenna Wollard was expected to again lead Purdue volleyball's hitting attack. Just ahead of the regular season, Wollard was mysteriously absent from the Boilermakers before posting on her Instagram account she was "currently dealing with an unexpected health issue that will keep me away for a little while." Wollard stated then she did not wish to share any more details at the time. On Thursday, Wollard shared more in-depth details. In August, Wollard was diagnosed with Non-Hodgkins Lymphoma, which she learned on Thursday is in remission. "These past couple months have been so tough, but hearing the news today brought so much joy," Wollard posted on Instagram. "I still have some treatments left, but I am very hopeful for what's ahead." Wollard returned to the Purdue bench on Sept. 2 for a short portion of the Boilermakers' win over Georgia. On Sept. 27, Wollard's return became more consistent. "Hopefully she can give us an emotional lift a little bit." Purdue enters Thursday's home match against Rutgers ranked 11th in the AVCA coaches poll with a 13-6 record. After Ajay Mitchell’s career-high 30 points led them to victory in their first game without Jalen Williams , Cason Wallace, and All-Star Chet Holmgren , the Oklahoma City Thunder suffered their first regular-season loss to the Dallas Mavericks. Without Wallace, Oklahoma City held All-Star Devin Booker to three points on 1-for-7 shooting but struggled to limit Flagg and Kyrie Irving’s offense, and Daigneault tipped his cap after the Thunder’s 26-point loss, per The Oklahoman’s Justin Martinez. “Credit Flagg with some of the shot-making. item.title: Nick Hardy cashes in as an alternate: Start in Mexico secures PGA Tour retirement vesting
item.description: Nick Hardy may have opened the VidantaWorld Mexico Open with a modest 1-under 70 on Thursday, but he was arguably the biggest winner on the PGA Tour. Hardy was simply grateful to be in the field after gaining entry as an alternate when Taylor Moore withdrew before his 8 a.m. tee time. He got Moore's spot in a grouping off No. 1 with Ben Martin and Kevin Roy. The start marked Hardy’s 15th Tour appearance of the season, enough to vest in the Tour’s retirement plan. “A lot of the decision to travel, talking with my wife about it, was to complete that goal because that was one of my goals this year, and that's today,” Hardy said. “So, I mean, it really couldn't have been a better day for me.” The 30-year-old, a one-time PGA Tour winner, has spent much of the season navigating life with limited status in the past champions category. He entered the week as the third alternate but decided Tuesday night it was worth the gamble to fly south of the border. “I've gone to tournaments and not gotten in, and I've gone to tournaments and gotten in as an alternate,” he said. “I just wanted to run my luck and see if it was going to happen. I didn't really know much, but I decided to come. “That's one of those weeks for me where a start means a lot, so why not go see if your number gets called?” Hardy went to bed early Wednesday night and awoke Thursday morning to a text informing him he had moved to first alternate because neither Luke List nor S.Y. Noh was on site. “Waking up with that news was nice,” Hardy said. It's been a difficult season for Hardy, who has split time between the PGA Tour and Korn Ferry Tour. He entered the week having made just four cuts in 14 PGA Tour starts and ranked 193rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings . “It totally sucks,” said Hardy, who finished 175th in the FedEx Cup standings in 2025 after struggling with his putting. “When I get in, I can't not play. item.title: Texas Tech paid Skydance Sports $999K to make Paramount+ docuseries about football program
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect A few months back, Paramount+ announced that The Program: Texas Tech , a four-part docuseries about the Red Raiders football program, would launch in September. That announcement wasn’t unusual, as docuseries that go inside a pro or sports franchise are all the rage these days. However, something was unusual about how this specific project came together. According to Daniel Libit at Sportico , Texas Tech paid Skydance Sports, the company’s sports-centric production studio, $999,999 to film the four-part series. Per a term sheet, the university agreed to pay a “studio fee” over three installments. The agreement doesn’t mention any potential revenue sharing from the docuseries to the school. The arrangement runs counter to how these deals usually work, with production companies typically compensating schools for access. Examples include Campfire Film & TV paying LSU $1 million for the rights to produce The Money Game documentary , and Michigan reportedly getting $2.25 million for the All or Nothing Amazon Prime documentary series, and EverWonder Studio agreeing to pay North Carolina at least $250,000 for a since-scrapped documentary series about Bill Belichick’s Tar Heels program. The term sheet, which was signed by Texas Tech president Lawrence Schovanec, gave Skydance’s producers access to “all of the team’s players and personnel,” as well as Galaxy Stadium, several facilities, NIL negotiations, coaches and GM meetings, practices, and training sessions. Texas Tech also provided a “dedicated production office” in its athletic complex. As for why the agreement was $999,999, Sportico noted that it kept the deal below the “major contract” threshold under Texas law, which could have subjected the public university to additional scrutiny and oversight, including Board of Regents approval. Texas Tech did retain limited review and approval rights over rough and final cuts to ensure it “does not portray TTU or its students, alumni, or employees in a manner giving rise to actionable defamation.” The agreement also gives the school the chance to request use of social media or short-form content produced by Skydance Sports six months after the final episode. Texas Tech has been pushing all its chips into the middle of the table in recent years as it tries to position itself among the country’s top college football programs. Clearly, they’re sparing no expense in that department, though the fact that they had to pay to play says a lot about how that push is going. item.title: £67m Germany midfielder is Liverpool's Alex Scott alternative
item.description: £67m Germany midfielder is Liverpool's Alex Scott alternative It’s no secret that Liverpool admire Alex Scott. The 23-year-old Bournemouth midfielder has previously worked with head coach Andoni Iraola at the Vitality Stadium. Now a fully established England international Scott has risen in prominence over the past year or so. The Cherries are desperate to tie the midfield dynamo down to a new deal - but if not then they will sell him to a top team for what could end up being a nine-figure fee. Alex Scott could go to Chelsea One issue for Liverpool is the presence of Chelsea in the race. Xabi Alonso’s side are now considered favourites to land the ex-Bristol City man. And should the Reds miss out on signing Scott then alternative names will have to be considered. According to a report in TEAMtalk it could prove to be the case that Felix Nmecha arrives from Borussia Dortmund next summer instead. “Liverpool have also got him listed, viewing him as a potential alternative should other targets like Alex Scott prove unattainable,” the report reads. Liverpool want Felix Nmecha instead of Alex Scott Nmecha, 26, joined the Yellow and Blacks from Wolfsburg back in 2023. He has risen in stature since then - becoming a full German international and a coveted prospect for many top English and European teams. Liverpool are listed alongside Manchester United as potentially interested in Nmecha - who is under contract at Signal Iduna Park until 2030. The deal he signed earlier in 2026 contains a release clause however - with €80m (£67m) the fee set for his signature in summer 2027. Before that and Liverpool - or anyone else for that matter - face paying an eye-watering €100m (£84m) fee for the midfielder. Nmecha's €80m release clause “An €80 million clause will only become available from the summer,” the report reads. “Until then, any buyer would need to meet Dortmund’s valuation, which sources place in the region of €100 million.” Losing out on Scott would be a bitter blow - particularly since Chelsea have enjoyed transfer successes against the Merseyside outfit over the past few seasons. But the acquisition of Nmecha - one of Europe’s most in-demand midfielders - would surely cushion the blow.

item.title: Sergio Garcia’s controversial comments during his final PGA Tour event shouldn’t be forgotten as he seeks return
item.description: Photo by Warren Little/Getty Images Sergio Garcia is seeking a return to the PGA Tour after officially confirming his exit from LIV Golf. Garcia left the PGA Tour to join LIV way back in June 2022 and up until the past few months, he has been one of the league’s loudest cheerleaders. He has also taken a seriously patronizing and, quite frankly, conceited stance against anyone who dared to speak out against LIV. However, now that LIV Golf is on its last legs, Sergio Garcia has announced his intentions to return to the PGA Tour. Garcia officially confirmed his exit from LIV on Thursday, while suggesting that he is keeping his ‘options open for a return to the PGA Tour’. I’m sorry Sergio, but you do not have that option. You lost that privilege four years ago after leaving the PGA Tour and speaking about it in such a detrimental manner. Sergio Garcia’s controversial comments during his final PGA Tour event During Garcia’s last official PGA Tour appearance outside of the majors at the Wells Fargo Championship in May 2022, he was caught on camera letting rip at the officials. “ I can’t wait to leave this tour, “ Garcia exclaimed. “ Can’t wait to get out of here. Just a couple more weeks until I don’t have to deal with [the rules officials] anymore.” I say Garcia has made his bed and now he should be made to lie in it. The only reason he has come crawling back now is because there will be seriously diminished purses on LIV 2.0 in 2027 as well as significantly weaker fields. The Spaniard knew exactly what he was doing when he joined LIV Golf in 2022, and indeed the risk attached to his decision. Aside from leaving the PGA Tour in order to join a rival organization, the 46-year-old has displayed some truly horrendous behavior out on the golf course, none more so than his angry outburst during the Masters earlier this year when he severely damaged a tee box at Augusta National. Professional golf does not need Sergio Garcia. In my opinion, he should be banned from ever playing on the PGA Tour again, as well as every other player who has decided to leave LIV Golf as soon as the Saudis pulled the plug on their financial backing.

item.title: MotoGP Today | Marquez and Martin address championship battle in Malaysia
item.description: Up next on the MotoGP calendar is the Malaysian Grand Prix. Ahead of the weekend, the two contenders for this year's title, Marc Marquez and Jorge Martin , discussed the impact of Martin's injury on the championship battle. During the Sprint at the Australian Grand Prix, Martin fell on Lap 8, and X-rays revealed a fracture of the radius in his forearm. The Aprilia rider will take part in FP1 on Friday, after which he will be assessed to determine whether he is fit to compete for the rest of the weekend. Currently, the gap between the two contenders stands at 10 points in favor of the defending world champion. Martin avoided losing further ground last Sunday, as the race had to be cancelled due to severe weather conditions. Speaking to DAZN in Sepang, Marquez joked about the situation the cancellation of the final race at Phillip Island: "I almost grabbed the car and went looking for the helicopter." On a more serious note, he added: "Whenever a race is cancelled for safety reasons, whether it gives you an advantage or not, you need to be able to accept it." Marquez also expects Martin to be fast if he is allowed to race this weekend. "I don’t think anyone, other than him and his team, knows the true extent of the injury. But to be honest, for the sake of the battle, he needs to be out there. And if he is truly fit, following the protocol that was applied after our incident in Qatar, then he is fit to race. And if he’s fit to race, Jorge Martin is a fast rider on track." Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Martin addresses his situation Speaking to the same Spanish broadcaster, the Aprilia rider said: "I’m here to give it a try. Afterward, I’ll make my next decision whether to continue with the Grand Prix. My expectations are quite low. I’ve done everything I could to arrive in the best possible condition. I’ll try to focus on riding and see how far I can go." He also highlighted that what's at stake makes him give it a go. "I’m here because a world championship is at stake. If there were nothing at stake, I’d go home, spend a month in a cast, and then perhaps return in Portimao, or maybe not. That’s what my body is telling me to do, and I’m certainly not in the best condition, but I believe I can make it that far and then see how to proceed." All eyes are on now the first practice session of the weekend. Moreover, Trackhouse's Raul Fernandez is in a similar situation, and will be evaluated after FP1.

item.title: Sunderland Are Eyeing A January Move For This Ligue 1 Winger: Good Fit For Le Bris?
item.description: Sunderland Are Eyeing A January Move For This Ligue 1 Winger: Good Fit For Le Bris? In a recent report , Foot Marseille stated that Sunderland are eyeing a January move for Olympique Marseille winger Igor Paixão. It has been mentioned that the Black Cats are planning to get a deal done for the Brazilian wide player in the winter transfer window. Paixao’s Impressive Form In Ligue 1 Paixao has caught the eye at times with his performances on the left side of Marseille’s attack this season. The Brazilian talent has participated in ten matches for the French outfit in this campaign so far, scoring two goals and earning one assist in various competitions. The 26-year-old is currently one of the most talented wingers in Ligue 1. Hence, Sunderland would do well to get a deal over the line for him this January. His current contract at the French club will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it difficult for the Black Cats to sign him on a cut-price deal in 2027. MARSEILLE, FRANCE – NOVEMBER 25: Igor Paixao of Olympique de Marseille runs with the ball during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD5 match between Olympique de Marseille and Newcastle United FC at Stade de Marseille on November 25, 2025 in Marseille, France. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) Will Paixao Be A Good Fit For Sunderland? Paixao is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet and can make a few driving runs with it out on the flanks. He has the eye to play some decisive passes in and around the opposition penalty area and can shoot the ball with power from long range. The Brazilian wide player can chip in by scoring and creating the odd goal for his side. Paixao is primarily a left-winger but can also serve as a right-sided wide player or play in the number ten position if asked to do so. However, there are some concerns on whether he can adapt to the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if the Black Cats manage to sign him next year. We can expect Paixao to bring more quality and depth to Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris’ frontline. He has what it takes to fight for a regular first-team spot at the Stadium of Light. At 26, Paixao has his peak years ahead of him, which makes him a decent fit for the Wearside club’s needs in 2027. Therefore, Le Bris would be wise to go all out to sign him soon.

item.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea as three more join penalty hall of shame | Football Daily
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily isn’t suggesting standards at Chelsea have slipped in recent years, but the quality of their players who miss penalties in shootouts against Liverpool certainly appears to be on the slide. Before last night, footballing royalty such as Arjen Robben, Geremi, Tammy Abraham, César Azpilicueta, Mason Mount and even goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga had all missed from the spot in four consecutive post-match deciders against Liverpool across 19 years and four different competitions. On Wednesday, a flame-haired Argentinian irritant, a striker we’d never previously heard of before yesterday and a defensive liability whose boots increasingly look to have been welded on to the wrong feet each added their names to the roll of shame. Valentín Barco, Emanuel Emegha and Wesley Fofana, take a collective bow. The reaction when Fleetwood made the final penalty was the best example I’ve ever seen of pandemonium ! – Jim Geissman A few random thoughts from one of the Wednesday fans who saw Harry Kane’s first goal at Orient ( Tuesday’s Football Daily ). Main after match conversation topics were how we’d shipped four goals in the second half, our new signing Gary Madine, and those people on the balconies of the new flats who watched the game for free. Without cameras I’d have no recall of Harry Kane’s goal but funnily enough I do genuinely remember Dean Cox having a very good game. We’ve talked about it loads since, but I don’t think any of us at the time thought Kane stood out in that game. Which just goes to show. A thoroughly deserved award for a career of consistent & often under-appreciated excellence. And what a superb motto: “Work in silence. Let success be your voice” – Alan. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
